issues.legal_issue: The effect of a decision in a succession-certificate proceeding on the trial of the same question in a later suit or proceeding between the same parties.
material_facts: A claimant sought a succession certificate to collect money owed to the deceased and also brought a suit seeking declaration of inheritance rights, partition, and possession of the estate against the same opposing parties.

The certificate proceeding and the suit were tried together. The specific dispute over whether the claimant’s status as a uterine brother entitled him to inherit was not raised as an issue in the certificate proceeding.
The High Court treated the certificate decision as res judicata in the suit and dismissed the second appeal on that ground.
issues.conclusion: The certificate decision did not bar trial of the same question in the suit. The High Court’s order was set aside and the case remanded for the second appeal to be decided on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Section 387 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 provides that a decision under Part X on a question of right between parties does not bar trial of the same question in a suit or other proceeding between them; it therefore excludes such decisions from the operation of Explanation VIII to Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Sections 372(3) and 373(3) provide for a limited, summary determination of entitlement to a certificate, including on a prima facie basis where questions are intricate or difficult; Section 381 gives the certificate its effect of protecting debtors or persons liable on securities who pay the certificate holder in good faith. Under Pawan Kumar Gupta v. Rochiram Nagdeo, res judicata attaches to a decision on an issue directly and substantially raised, not an incidental finding. Kalipada De v. Dwijapada Das did not assist the claimant because the relevant inheritance issue had not been raised in the certificate proceeding. The limited nature of the inquiry and the rule in Section 387 are consistent with Mt. Charjo v. Dina Nath, which recognised that a certificate does not finally settle competing heirs’ rights or bar a regular suit.

predicates.succession_certificate_proceeding: A party sought a certificate to collect a deceased person’s debts or securities.
predicates.same_question_between_same_parties: The same question of right arose between the same parties in both proceedings.
predicates.later_suit_or_proceeding: A party brought a later suit or other proceeding in which that question was to be tried.

issues.definition: When a certificate proceeding and a later proceeding involve the same question between the same parties, the decision in the certificate proceeding does not prevent that question from being tried in the later proceeding.
